episodes.name: Tribute to The Troops (2010)
episodes.overview:
No one deserves our thanks more than the brave men and women who serve in our Armed Forces. That’s why Slim Jim and WWE are joining forces to pay Tribute to the Troops. You can do your part by saying "thank you" with an e-mail or a letter to a member of the U.S. Military, or by helping Slim Jim donate snacks. Buy two Slim Jims today, and Slim Jim will donate one back to the troops.

The eighth annual WWE Tribute to the Troops holiday special featured Superstars from both Raw and SmackDown, along with appearances by special celebrity guests such as Sean "Diddy" Combs' Diddy-Dirty Money, King of Comedy Cedric the Entertainer, The View's Sherri Shepherd, Miss USA Rima Fakih and many others. Check out exclusive photos, videos and more from the most patriotic show of the year.

episodes.name: Tribute to the Troops (2011)
episodes.overview:
The event was taped December 11, 2011 in Fayetteville, North Carolina at the Crown Coliseum, the taping was performed in front of U.S. military service members from the nearby Fort Bragg military base and their families.[12]This is also the first Tribute to the Troops that was taped indoors rather than outdoors.

The event featured a pre-recorded message from President Barack Obama. Nickelback performed the clean version of Burn It to the Ground, the theme song for Raw SuperShow, and When We Stand Together. Sgt. Slaughter made a special appearance. George Wallace performed some stand-up comedy. Mary J. Blige performed Need Someone and Family Affair.
